investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-31T14:32 with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api layer could not reach the swarm backend ELB at /v1/agents during agent provisioning. Because the failure occurs at the very first network hop to the swarm gateway — before any agent identity, VM ID, or state is returned — all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent and every downstream contract assertion is unverifiable.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting /v1/agents) was unreachable from the production-api at the time of the eval run. The production-api returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" on every POST /api/agents attempt, preventing agent provisioning from starting and leaving the eval with an empty evidence object. Because all three sibling checks share the identical error message and all failed within the same ~35-second window, the failure is localized to the shared swarm gateway dependency, not to any individual check's logic or eval runner code.

investigation.title: image-generation-stream eval failure: OpenAI API credit balance exhausted on /api/generate/image/stream
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API key used by the eval runner has no remaining credits, causing the upstream image generation call to return a credit_balance_exhausted error. The stream terminated with a generation_error frame instead of the required generation_completed frame, so both contract assertions (frameTypes contains "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent equals true) were violated. This is an eval infrastructure failure caused by an exhausted external API billing account; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The OpenAI organization account whose API key is configured for the eval runner has exhausted its credit balance. When the runner called /api/generate/image/stream (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1984), the AURA backend forwarded the request to OpenAI, which rejected it with HTTP error type "insufficient_quota" and code "credit_balance_exhausted". The stream emitted generation_start and generation_progress frames before receiving the error, then emitted a generation_error frame and terminated without ever emitting generation_completed or an image URL. Both required contract assertions therefore failed. The failure is localized to the eval runner's OpenAI billing account and the /api/generate/image/stream endpoint; no evidence of a code defect or configuration regression is present.

possibleCauses: Primary (high confidence): The OpenAI API key or organization account used by the eval runner has a zero or negative credit balance, causing all image generation requests to be rejected immediately with credit_balance_exhausted.

investigations.rootCause: The AURA runtime API endpoint POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test returned HTTP 502 for model aura-gpt-5-5. The 502 body contains a nested 424 Failed Dependency with error code provider_account_unavailable and the message "AURA is temporarily unable to reach the model provider. This indicates that at the time of the eval run (2026-08-31T14:31:36Z), the upstream provider backing aura-gpt-5-5 was unreachable from AURA's backend, causing the harness runtime test to fail with llm_error. The eval infrastructure correctly detected and recorded the failure; the root cause is an upstream provider connectivity or availability issue for the aura-gpt-5-5 model, not a defect in the eval runner or contract definitions.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-31T14:32 with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api layer could not reach the swarm backend ELB at /v1/agents during agent provisioning. investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting /v1/agents) was unreachable from the production-api at the time of the eval run. The production-api returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" on every POST /api/agents attempt, preventing agent provisioning from starting and leaving the eval with an empty evidence object. Because all three sibling checks share the identical error message and all failed within the same ~35-second window, the failure is localized to the shared swarm gateway dependency, not to any individual check's logic or eval runner code.
